deep.reconstruction: Euler writes ∫1/z^a for the full power sum Σ_{z≥1} z^{-a} = ζ(a). He writes ∫1/z^a (1/y^b) for the nested 'singular' series Σ_z z^{-a} Σ_{y<z} y^{-b}, a double zeta (Euler) sum. The page sits in §§7–8 of E477, the founding paper on double zeta values. In §7 Euler expands each term by partial fractions of 1/(z^m y^n), with telescoping/Abel-type rearrangement. He then expresses ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) as two 'parts'. The previous page gives the part generated with binomial coefficients C(m+k−1,k): Σ_k (−1)^k C(m+k−1,k)(1±(−1)^k·1) ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) ∓ Σ_k C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k, n−k). The upper signs hold for m even, the lower for m odd. This page completes §7 with the symmetric 'Pars altera', obtained by m↔n, with signs governed by the parity of n. §8 then specialises. For m even, the factor (1+1)=2 survives only for even k and (1−1)=0 kills the odd-k product terms. Pars prima then becomes 2ζ(m)ζ(n) + 2C(m+1,2)ζ(m+2)ζ(n−2) + 2C(m+3,4)ζ(m+4)ζ(n−4) + … − Σ_k C(m+k−1,k) ζ(m+k, n−k). The next page displays this. The purpose is the classical result: when m+n is odd, the double sums can be eliminated in favour of products of ordinary zeta values. This yields closed forms for ζ(m,n) of odd weight.
errors: In the last displayed line of 'Pars prima si m sit numerus par' the printed coefficient is (m+1)(m+2)/(1·2·3). The pattern, the previous page and the next page all require m(m+1)(m+2)/(1·2·3); the factor m is dropped, a typographical slip.
Gap (not an error): the series formally run over k = 0,1,2,…. Their termination (n−k ≥ 1, or the convergence restrictions on the ζ(n−k) and ζ(m+k, n−k) involved) is not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Expression of ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) as binomially weighted sums of products ζ(m+k)ζ(n−k) and double sums ζ(m+k, n−k), split into two symmetric parts with parity-dependent signs
ideas.modern_name: Euler's decomposition / reduction formula for double zeta values (partial-fraction relation; precursor of the double-shuffle relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E477 (1776); revived by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn, Zagier, Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Parity simplification: factors (1±1) annihilate alternate terms according to whether m (resp. n) is even or odd
ideas.modern_name: Parity reduction leading to evaluation of odd-weight double zeta values
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477); modern proofs by Borwein–Girgensohn and others

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known core computation of E477, the paper universally cited as the origin of double zeta values and Euler's odd-weight evaluation. Nothing here is absent from the modern literature; the only notable item is a dropped factor m in one coefficient.
transcription_corrections: Pars altera, second row: the second sign should read '∓ n/1 ∫1/z^{n+1}(1/y^{m−1})' (as in the image and the parallel Pars prior), not '±'.
Pars altera, fourth row: likewise '∓ n(n+1)(n+2)/1·2·3 ∫…', not '±'.

Last formula of Pars prima (m even): the image reads '−(m+1)(m+2)/1.2.3 ∫1/z^{m+3}(1/y^{n−3})'. The exponent smudge 'm+13' is m+3. The coefficient as printed lacks m (a printing error, not a transcription error).
